subject: HelixBio pilot — request for volume breakpoint concession
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Park <samantha@helixbio.com>, Paul Lee <paul.lee@helixbio.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HelixBio pilot — initial packaging proposal

Hi Samantha / Paul,

Thanks again for a great conversation this morning. Quick recap and the packaging we discussed for the 6-month pilot:

- Pilot scope: clinical-note summarization (4 models), up to ~2B tokens/month peak, expected average 800M tokens/month.
- Proposed packaging: 6-month pilot, month-to-month billing, committed minimum of 3 months. 
- Pricing recommendation (attachment): base list rate with pilot concession = 25% off list for the first 3 months, then 15% for months 4–6.

They asked about a deeper breakpoint once they move to volume — specifically a one-time higher discount threshold if they hit >=8B tokens/month within the pilot window. They want the option to trigger a steeper per-token credit retroactive to the start of the month.

Before I reply to their exact ask, I want to check what sign-off we need to offer: a conditional breakpoint credit vs. an up-front deeper discount. Can we do a contingent credit structure (e.g., 30% credit on overage tokens retroactive for the month they cross 8B) with a total credit cap?

Attached: proposed_pricing_sheet.xlsx (proposal with modeled ARR/credit scenarios), usage_forecast_helixbio.csv

Key asks from me:
- Permission to offer a contingent breakpoint credit up to a hard cap of $150k, or
- Guidance to propose an alternate (e.g., higher upfront discount for first 3 months but no retroactive credit).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if useful. I want to close pilot terms this week.

Best,
Jonas Weber

Jonas — thanks for the recap and for the fast turnaround on the attachment. 

Two quick clarifications from our side:
1) The 8B-trigger is important to us because of expected burst months when ongoing clinical ingestion hits a new data source. If we hit that volume within month 2 or 3, we'd want the per-token price to step down retroactively for that month.
2) Can you confirm whether the credit is limited to pilot usage (i.e., not applied to post-pilot committed volumes)?

If you can provide a simple conditional example (numbers) showing the delta between a) upfront deeper discount, and b) retroactive credit with a cap, that would help our procurement team move faster. We are hoping to get legal/finance input this week and would prefer a structure that avoids lengthier redlines.

— Samantha

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: HelixBio pilot — request for volume breakpoint concession (requesting approval)

Marissa / Grace — forwarding the thread with HelixBio. They asked for a retroactive breakpoint at 8B tokens/month during the pilot. I ran the numbers in the attached sheet and modeled three options:

Option A (Conservative): No retroactive credit. Offer 30% off list for months 1–3, then 20% for months 4–6. No retroactive adjustments. Estimated pilot cost to Helix (6 months): $198k.

Option B (Contingent credit — preferred by customer): Standard pilot discount (25% months 1–3), and add a retroactive credit of 30% applied to token usage in any month they cross 8B tokens, capped at $150k total credit across the pilot. This is the structure Samantha asked us to consider.

Option C (Aggressive upfront): 35% off list for first 3 months, 25% months 4–6, no retroactive credit; no cap needed.

Commercial impact notes (from modeled sheet):
- If Helix hits 8B/month once during pilot, Option B reduces revenue vs Option A by ~$95–120k depending on exact usage curve. If they never hit 8B, Option B is roughly equivalent to Option A.
- Biggest risk with Option B is open-ended retro activity; cap mitigates that.

Request: approval to offer Option B with the following constraints:
- Hard credit cap = $150,000 for the pilot (applies retroactively if trigger crossed).
- Credit applies only to pilot invoices; post-pilot committed pricing must be negotiated separately.
- Require legal to add explicit trigger language and usage verification steps (we will require Helix to provide logs, and we will audit usage).

Attachments included: proposed_pricing_sheet.xlsx, term_sheet_redline.pdf

Can you confirm whether finance sign-off is needed vs. VP commercial? If you ok this, I will respond to Samantha with the structure and the cap.

Thanks,
Jonas

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: HelixBio pilot — request for volume breakpoint concession (requesting approval)

Jonas — thanks for the clear breakdown and the modeling. A few points from rev ops/finance perspective: 

- I support Option B on the basis we keep a hard cap and require an auditable verification process. The $150k cap is within a tolerable range given the deal size and strategic value.
- Please add a clause that credits are applied only after Redwood confirms usage via our ingestion logs (we should not rely solely on vendor-supplied numbers).
- Require monthly checkpoints and a clause to revisit pricing at pilot close (so we don't lock post-pilot pricing).

Action items before I sign off:
1) Updated term_sheet_redline.pdf with explicit trigger/cap language (agree to draft).
2) Revenue ops to confirm accounting treatment for retro credits (I will loop in Erin in my next message).

If Grace is comfortable with the commercial trade-off, I can route this to VP for final approval if needed. Jonas — please prepare the short one-pager I can send to finance with the ask summarized.

— Marissa
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: HelixBio pilot — request for volume breakpoint concession (requesting approval)

Marissa / Jonas — I agree with moving forward on Option B with the following limits to control risk: 

- Approve contingent retro credit at 30% with a hard pilot cap = $120,000 (vs. the $150k proposed).
- Require the clause that credits are only applied after Redwood verification and that credits cannot be applied to any SaaS addons or professional services — token-only.
- Add a quarterly review clause if the pilot extends >6 months.

Jonas: please send Samantha the Option B structure with the $120k cap and note that this needs legal language and finance confirmation before being binding. If Helix accepts the structure in principle, we'll get legal to prepare a slim addendum and finance to confirm accounting.

Thanks — Grace
